title: The Knowledge of the Holy
author: A. W. Tozer
edition_analyzed: First edition (with references to modern reprints for context)
target_audience: Christians seeking deeper understanding of God
Students of Christian spirituality and doctrine
General readers interested in classic Christian literature
core_themes: The majesty and mystery of God's nature
Recovering reverence and awe toward God
The relationship between knowledge of God and practical Christian living
The importance of correct theology for worship and faith
primary_purpose: To deepen readers’ understanding and reverence for God by exploring His essential attributes and countering the diminishing view of God in modern Christianity.

structure_format.narrative_style: Reverent, devotional, yet intellectually rigorous and concise
structure_format.organization: 22 brief chapters, each focusing on a specific attribute of God, with a preface and closing prayer

key_concepts_lessons: A diminished view of God leads to spiritual decline.
God’s attributes—such as omniscience, sovereignty, and immutability—are foundational to Christian belief.
Every doctrine and action in Christian life flows from understanding who God is.
True worship arises from an accurate conception of God.
God’s nature is ultimately incomprehensible, but He reveals enough for faith and devotion.
Reverence, awe, and humility are essential responses to God's majesty.
notable_features: Classic devotional approach with theological depth
Each chapter ends with a short prayer of adoration or supplication
Enduring influence in evangelical and broader Christian circles
Citations of both Scripture and church fathers
cultural_historical_context: Published in early 1960s America amid growing concerns about secularism, theological liberalism, and the loss of transcendence in Christian worship. Tozer calls for a return to a God-centered faith and reverence.
reception_impact: Enduring classic in devotional and theological literature
Widely praised for its depth, clarity, and devotional warmth
Frequently used in seminars, Bible studies, and personal reflection
Recognized for reigniting interest in the attributes of God among evangelicals
Cited as formative by numerous Christian leaders
comparable_titles: Knowing God by J. I. Packer
The Pursuit of God by A. W. Tozer
Attributes of God by A. W. Pink
The Holiness of God by R. C. Sproul
